title: Finite flat surjections are surjective on $k$-points
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed and $f:X\to Y$ a finite flat
surjective morphism of schemes of finite type over $k$. Then
$f(X(k))=Y(k)$.

proof.text:
Let $y\in Y(k)$. The fibre $X_y=X\times_Yy$ is nonempty
(surjectivity), finite and flat over $k$, hence a nonempty finite
$k$-scheme, which has a $k$-point by
[lem-sc-finite-nonempty-point]; such a point is an
$x\in X(k)$ with $f(x)=y$.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed and $f:X\to Y$ a finite surjective
morphism of schemes. Then every morphism $y:\Spec k\to Y$ lifts to a
morphism $x:\Spec k\to X$ with $f\circ x=y$. In particular, if $f$ is
a morphism of $k$-schemes, then $f(X(k))=Y(k)$.

proof.text:
Let $y:\Spec k\to Y$. The fibre $X_y=X\times_{Y,y}\Spec k$ is finite
over $k$, being a base change of $f$, and nonempty, since $f$ is
surjective and a base change of a surjective morphism is surjective.
So it is a nonempty finite $k$-scheme, which has a $k$-point
$s:\Spec k\to X_y$ by [lem-sc-finite-nonempty-point]. The composite
$x$ of $s$ with the projection $X_y\to X$ satisfies $f\circ x=y$. If
$f$ is a morphism of $k$-schemes and $y$ is a $k$-point, then $x$ is a
$k$-point as well, because the structure morphism of $X$ is that of $Y$
composed with $f$.
